predecessors.name: Assyria
predecessors.text: the Assyrian heartland of the Middle Assyrian Empire

successors.name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
successors.text: the Assyrian heartland, Harran and the lands west of the Euphrates ("Transpotamia") and the Levant that "had been split between Babylon and the Medes"

successors.name: Median Kingdom
successors.text: the northern Zagros mountains, which the Medes received

successors.name: Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt
successors.text: Egypt, independent from about 655 BC under Psamtik I

ledger.x: 911 BC: Adad-nirari II becomes king of Assyria and the Neo-Assyrian Empire begins.
Cliopatria's -900 shape is 250,500 km2, ten times the heartland.
ledger.cp: Aramean kingdoms and tribes (page silent on names)

ledger.x: 894 BC: Guzana pays tribute.
879 BC: Ashurnasirpal II makes Nimrud the capital.
857/856 BC: Bit Adini falls.
808 BC: the tribute of Guzana ends in annexation (next event).
808 BC: Guzana becomes an Assyrian province.
Cliopatria widens the shape at -800 by 222,552 km2 (west to 34.5 E, south to 31.2 N).
ledger.cp: Aram-Damascus and the western states (page silent)

ledger.x: 773 BC: Damascus pays tribute.
740 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Arpad.
738 BC: new provinces in Syria.
738 BC: Hama is left as a vassal.
734 BC: Gaza falls and Assyria borders Egypt.
After 734 BC: "Asqaluna, Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon, and the Mu’na Arab tribe, all began paying tribute."
732 BC: the tribute of Damascus ends in annexation (next event).
732 BC: Damascus falls.
732 BC: southern Israel becomes a vassal.
729 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Babylon.
The 720s: Samaria falls.
The 720s: Samaria becomes an Assyrian province.
Early 721 BC: Marduk-apla-iddina seizes Babylon.
720 BC: Hama is annexed.
720 BC: Sargon II annexes Hama again after the battle of Qarqar on the Orontes.
717 BC: Sargon II retakes Carchemish.
713 BC: Sargon II annexes Tabal.
710 BC: Sargon II conquers Babylonia again.
709 BC: Cyprus is absorbed.
694 BC (bridged): Chaldea is subjugated.
Esarhaddon "conquered the Phoenician city of Sidon, which was renamed Kar-Aššur‐aḫu‐iddina".
By 672 BC: the Scythians of West Asia become an Assyrian vassal.
671 BC: the Assyrian conquest of Egypt begins in earnest.
671 BC: Memphis falls.
669 BC: Taharqa retakes the Delta.
668 BC: Babylonia passes from direct Assyrian rule to a king of its own under Ashurbanipal.
668 BC: Shamash-shum-ukin "was relegated to being Ashurbanipal's closely monitored vassal".
667 BC: Ashurbanipal wins it back.

c. 664 BC: Tantamani recovers Memphis. Taharqa died in 664 and "his nephew Tantamani proclaimed himself pharaoh"; neither page opened here says he retook Memphis, which comes from the kingdom-of-kush dossier.
664 BC: Psamtik becomes an Assyrian vassal.
663 BC: Ashurbanipal defeats Tantamani.
663 BC: the Assyrian conquest ends.
663 BC: the Delta goes to the vassal state.

c. 655 BC: Egypt leaves Assyria. "Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE"; "Egypt already regained independence in the middle of Ashurbanipal's reign". Egypt's Twenty-sixth Dynasty continues the land.
653 BC: Assyria occupies Susa without annexing Elam.
652 BC: the vassal king rises against his brother.
652 BC: Shamash-shum-ukin revolts.
648 BC: Ashurbanipal takes Babylon.
648 BC: Babylonia becomes an Assyrian vassal kingdom.
646 BC (bridged): the occupation of Susa closes with the last dated Assyrian act there.
645 BC: Urartu becomes a dependent of Assyria, not a province.
635 BC (bridged): the end of Sarduri III's reign.

Nov. 626 BC: Babylon is lost for good. "Nabopolassar was formally invested as king of Babylon in November 626 BCE, restoring Babylonia as an independent kingdom"; the city "was seized by Nabopolassar in 626 and never again fell into Assyrian hands".

Nov. 626 BC: Nabopolassar's revolt takes ground. "Nippur was recaptured in October 626 BCE" and he "was formally invested as king of Babylon in November 626 BCE"; Neo-Babylonian page: "In 626 BC, Nabopolassar assaulted and successfully seized the cities of Babylon and Nippur". He held only these…
625 BC (bridged): the Scythian tie ends.
620 BC: the fighting for Babylonia ends.
620 BC: Babylonia is lost for good.
Late 615 or 614 BC: the Medes take Assur.
612 BC: Nineveh falls.
The tributaries of 734 (Judah, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Ashkelon) are closed at the empire's end; the pages give no year when each stopped paying.
609 BC (bridged): the west passes to Babylon.
609 BC: the Assyrian state ends at Harran.

wars.name: Ahuni and the conquest of Bit Adini
wars.outcome: "Ahuni of Bit Adini resisted for several years, but he surrendered to Shalmaneser in the winter of 857/856 BCE."

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar
wars.outcome: "In 853 BCE, a coalition of western states assembled at Tell Qarqur in Syria against Assyrian expansion"; Assyrian forces "thrice tried to capture Damascus but were unsuccessful" (undated).

wars.name: Shamshi-ilu's wars with Urartu and Damascus
wars.outcome: "In 774 BCE, Shamshi-ilu scored an important victory against Argishti I of Urartu", who was "not decisively beaten"; "Shamshi-ilu captured Damascus in 773 BCE and secured tribute".

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's Syrian and Levantine campaigns
wars.outcome: Arpad fell in 740 after a three-year siege and became two provinces; Hama became a vassal in 738; Gaza fell in 734; Damascus and the northern half of Israel were annexed in 732.

wars.name: Fall of Samaria
wars.outcome: Probably taken by Shalmaneser V in the 720s; "Sargon claimed to have conquered the city".

wars.name: Revolt of Hama and the Battle of Qarqar (720)
wars.outcome: Sargon beat Yahu-Bihdi's coalition at Qarqar on the Orontes and annexed Hama again; Hanunu of Gaza rebelled in the same period.

wars.name: Sargon II's Urartu campaign
wars.outcome: "The 714 campaign put an end to direct confrontations between Urartu and Assyria for the rest of Sargon's reign"; Musasir was plundered.

wars.name: Sargon II's Cyprus expedition
wars.outcome: "In 709, Assyria sent an expedition to Cyprus"; seven kings of Ia' were beaten and "Cyprus was thus absorbed into the Assyrian Empire".

wars.name: Sennacherib's Levantine campaign
wars.outcome: "In 701 BCE Sennacherib undertook the most famous campaign of his reign, invading the Levant"; the page gives no territorial result (Judah is a tributary).

wars.name: Sennacherib's Elamite and Babylonian wars
wars.outcome: "In 694 BCE Sennacherib invaded Elam"; "Sennacherib finally recaptured Babylon in 689 BCE," and "Babylon was destroyed".

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Memphis fell in 671, the Delta swung in 669 and 667, Psamtik became a vassal in 664, Tantamani was beaten in 663; "The Neo-Assyrian Empire vassalised Egypt for a period of about 10 years".

wars.name: Assyrian wars with Elam
wars.outcome: "Elam was defeated in a series of conflicts in 665, 653 and 647–646"; Susa was "captured and devastated"; but "Ashurbanipal did not annex Elam, instead leaving it to its own devices".

wars.name: Revolt of Shamash-shum-ukin
wars.outcome: Ashurbanipal captured Babylon in 648 after a siege of two years; Kandalanu was installed as vassal king.

wars.name: Fall of the Assyrian Empire
wars.outcome: Nabopolassar won Babylon (626), the Medes took Assur (614), the Medes and Babylonians took Nineveh (612), and Ashur-uballit II was beaten at Harran in 609.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate; the Egyptian border of 734 ("as far south as the border of Egypt") and the Median-Babylonian partition are the only lines the pages mention.
